small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose3d is almost certainly the dominant cost here (fast_p≈0.43, runtime 22ms vs baseline 9.4ms — the torch baseline itself runs the conv, so our overhead must come from softmax pass being slow or extra passes). Try collapsing the softmax to a single-pass online algorithm per (B,C) row when S fits — at S = D'·H'·W' = 32·64·64 = 131072 it doesn't fit in one block, so keep the 3-pass but increase TILE to 16384 or 32768 with num_warps=16 and num_stages=3 to reduce launch + memory traffic.
- Fuse the clamp into the conv_transpose epilogue rather than re-reading x in both stats and finalize kernels; alternatively, store the clamped tensor once into a scratch buffer so the finalize pass only does exp+scale instead of reload+clamp+exp.
- Add `triton.autotune` over TILE ∈ {4096, 8192, 16384, 32768} × num_warps ∈ {4,8,16} for both tile_stats and finalize kernels.
large_guidance:
- The real bottleneck is `nn.ConvTranspose3d` — at output shape (32,64,32,64,64) with k=3, stride=2 it dominates wall time. Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, OC_tile, output spatial tile), gathering the contributing input positions via the stride/padding/output_padding index math, and fuse clamp+exp(−gmax) prep into the epilogue. This is the highest-headroom move.
- Better: implement conv_transpose3d as a gather-based GEMM where each output voxel (od,oh,ow) computes which (id,ih,iw, kd,kh,kw) input/kernel pairs contribute (the "transposed conv as gather" formulation). Then fuse clamp directly into the GEMM epilogue, write to a scratch buffer, and run the existing two-pass softmax+scale on it.
- Fold the AvgPool3d into the conv_transpose input load path: since pool_kernel=2 with no overlap, the conv kernel can read 8 input voxels and average them inline instead of materializing the pooled tensor. This removes one full pass over a 32×32×32×64×64 tensor.
